questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Papua New Guinea about 462,840 square kilometres; Vietnam about 331,690 square kilometres; Suriname about 163,270 square kilometres; Switzerland about 41,291 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: True or false: “The capital city of Papua New Guinea is Phnom Penh.”

hints.nudge: Read the statement slowly. Does it match what the article says, or has one word been swapped for another?
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Papua New Guinea article, or on the Atlas.

questions.proof: The capital city of Papua New Guinea is Port Moresby.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Papua New Guinea?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Papua New Guinea article.

questions.proof: The capital city of Papua New Guinea is Port Moresby.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Papua New Guinea?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Papua New Guinea is the kina.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Port Moresby?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Papua New Guinea is Port Moresby.
